correctness.rationale: For all n≥2, every putative shattered five-query support has a 2-vertex cover, at most seven active points and at most 29 traces, so VC≤4. At n=7, the four-query active graph must have five active points and a degree-one vertex, which forces a trace collision. Explicit stars give VC lower bounds at n=4,5,6,8. In any adaptive root zero branch, a second query has a child with at most four hypotheses or a fixed-center star, both with Littlestone dimension at most two; thus overall Ldim≤4. A complete depth-four tree with sixteen distinct terminals on n=7 was checked path by path; small orders have independent counting upper bounds. Full direct finite recurrences corroborated n≤14. Every part is a proof or complete finite witness, not an extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The explicit family has a nontrivial and isolated one-order adaptive excess. Direct comparison with the closest 2020 Johnson-neighborhood full text, 2024 graph VC computation paper, 2022 general hardness results, related neighborhood literature, and semantic mathematical record searches did not identify an exact KG(n,2) open-neighborhood VC/Littlestone classification. Johnson J(n,2) open neighborhoods are not KG(n,2) open neighborhoods: the latter are complements of the former's closed neighborhoods. The 2020 paper Theorem 3.7 gives a different rank-two Johnson open VC threshold (four already at n=7). Historical-priority risk remains.
residual_risks: Historical priority is not guaranteed; equivalent results may be indexed under closed triangular-graph neighborhoods, pair-disjointness matrices or thicket dimension.
General graph-neighborhood computation papers might encode the finite VC values implicitly as a computation, though not as the exact all-parameter structural theorem.
Not every page of all related original papers was manually re-read; negative relevance assessment is limited to material actually inspected.

value.rationale: This gives a complete family-wide classification of static and online shattering for the natural disjointness graph on two-element subsets, and isolates a single strict adaptive gap on exactly 21 graph vertices. The VC proof is a structural 2-cover/trace argument; the online upper bound is uniform and the lone exceptional lower bound has an explicit certificate. The exact order of the first and only separation is mathematical content, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
